statement: Docker consumes the complete npm-owned production dependency tree without package-internal pruning, ordinary safety-spine tests reject post-install mutation, and the change-proof orchestrator provides an explicit full-proof execution handoff used by Solver and CI for known release-surface changes while unknown scope and invalid proof authority still refuse without execution.

constraints.statement: npm owns installed package internals; the selector owns proof requirements; the orchestrator alone executes them. Do not reconstruct these decisions in Solver or workflow YAML.

Keep ordinary modular refusal and side-effect-free explain/list modes. An explicit execution option may run check:release only for the authoritative RELEASE_PROOF_REQUIRED result. Unknown or invalid scope must refuse, including mixed changes.

Own Docker packaging, the selector-to-executor-to-Solver/CI handoff, their tests, release/workflow documentation and generated metadata. Preserve SQL behavior, all existing test gates and publication credentials.

Retain the predecessor Docker red regression, both production SQL dialect witnesses, independent packaging review and required static/change proof. Do not claim a structural witness proves a built image.
Never move existing tags or bypass gates. Publish the repaired exact commit, obtain exact-SHA CI and preflight, then ship the next 0.2 patch through the existing artifact publisher.
